amp.headerSubtitle: A single-ended, high-performance headphone amplifier — fully SMD on a 4-layer PCB, with a hybrid JFET + TPA6120 topology and a symmetrical battery power supply.
amp.aboutP1: NyaaHibiV2 builds on the topology of the first-generation amplifier, -NyaaHibi-. The name NyaaHibi itself comes from Japanese: Nyaa (にゃあ), meaning a cat's meow, and Hibi (日々), meaning every day. Combined, NyaaHibi can be read as "meowing every day" — a simple philosophy of bringing enjoyable sound that can be savored every day ^_^.
amp.aboutP2: In version V2, the design is fully SMD with several improvements — most notably, the final stage now uses the TPA6120A2 IC. The PCB is also upgraded to 4 layers for cleaner routing and lower noise. The circuit topology has been refined as well, improving sound quality while keeping the amplifier stable.
amp.topologyAlt: Block diagram of the NyaaHibiV2 amplifier

ampBlocks.title: Discrete JFET Input
ampBlocks.desc: Used to reduce the shortcomings of SMD input capacitors — the design is fully SMD, so large film capacitors like Wima aren't an option. JFETs also give a more "tube-ish" character, as their transfer curve resembles a vacuum tube.

ampBlocks.title: BJT Current Booster
ampBlocks.desc: Because a JFET's current capability is limited, BJT transistors are added as a current boost so the following stage can operate optimally.

ampBlocks.title: Outer Loop Preamp Gain
ampBlocks.desc: The main voltage gain stage of the system — it largely determines the amplifier's character or tonal color.

ampBlocks.title: Inner Loop Nested Feedback
ampBlocks.desc: Keeps the circuit stable despite the high gain of the preamp gain stage, minimizing phase shift.

ampBlocks.title: Buffer Frontend
ampBlocks.desc: Isolates the preamp gain block from the final stage so they don't affect each other.

ampBlocks.title: Front End Final Stage
ampBlocks.desc: Uses a composite amplifier concept to help correct the signal before it reaches the final output stage.

ampBlocks.title: Final Stage (TPA6120)
ampBlocks.desc: Uses the TPA6120 IC, known for its high slew rate, wide bandwidth, and excellent performance in headphone amplifier applications.

ampBlocks.title: DC Servo
ampBlocks.desc: Used because the design omits a DC blocking capacitor in the signal path. The DC servo keeps the output DC offset low without affecting the sound character.

amp.psuAlt: Block diagram of the NyaaHibiV2 power supply

psuBlocks.title: Charger Module
psuBlocks.desc: Uses a TP4056 module mounted onboard to save PCB space.

psuBlocks.title: Active Bypass Charging
psuBlocks.desc: While the battery charges, the amplifier draws power directly from the charger. This keeps the charging module from being overloaded when the amplifier is on. Switching uses a MOSFET to reduce power loss compared with conventional diodes.

psuBlocks.title: Step-Up Converter
psuBlocks.desc: Raises the battery voltage, with high- and low-voltage modes. Low mode gives longer runtime, while high mode delivers maximum performance.

psuBlocks.title: Charge Pump
psuBlocks.desc: Generates a negative voltage rail so the power supply becomes symmetrical (+ and −).

psuBlocks.title: Filter Stage 1
psuBlocks.desc: A combination of capacitor, ferrite bead, resistor, and capacitor that dampens initial ripple and noise.

psuBlocks.title: Capacitance Multiplier
psuBlocks.desc: Makes a small SMD capacitance behave like a large one, keeping the supply cleaner.

psuBlocks.title: Filter Stage 2
psuBlocks.desc: A local filter placed near each IC to reduce noise picked up from long supply traces.

microamp.aboutP1: MicroHibi was born from a simple idea: a headphone amplifier that still sounds good but is truly tiny. The project focuses on an amplifier that is practical for everyday use without carrying large equipment. The result is MicroHibi — a portable amplifier about 5 cm × 2,5 cm that is easy to take anywhere.
microamp.aboutP2: The name MicroHibi itself comes from the previous project, NyaaHibi. If NyaaHibi is the larger version, then MicroHibi can be seen as its tiny counterpart with the same philosophy: simple and compact, while still keeping a serious design approach to the circuit — including a power supply topology that is not cut down from the previous version.
microamp.infoP1: Because it is extremely small and uses a mini battery, output power is naturally not as large as a desktop amplifier. MicroHibi uses a symmetric 5V supply that is very power-efficient and suits batteries around 500 mAh. To keep headphones safe, the circuit is also equipped with a DC Servo that keeps DC offset low without affecting the amplifier's sound character.
microamp.infoP2: The MicroHibi circuit is essentially inspired by the standard OCL (Output Capacitor-Less) amplifier topology commonly used in audio amplifiers. However, so it could fit on a much smaller PCB, several parts of the circuit were simplified and adjusted without changing its core operating principles.
microamp.infoP3: One of the changes is in the bias network. Classic OCL designs usually use a diode as the bias regulator for the output stage, but in MicroHibi this part is replaced with a transistor. Besides helping keep bias stable, this approach also allows a more compact circuit that is easier to implement on a small PCB.
microamp.infoP4: With this approach, MicroHibi keeps the core character of the classic amplifier topology, with a few adjustments to make it more suitable for portable devices. The goal is a circuit that stays simple, efficient with space, and still delivers good audio performance in a very compact size.

ampBlocks.title: SE Buffer PNP
ampBlocks.desc: Acts as the initial buffer stage, isolating the signal source from the main amplifier stage so input impedance stays high. This stage also has local negative feedback, which helps correct distortion early on and keeps the loop stable before the signal enters the next gain stage.

ampBlocks.title: VAS (Voltage Amplifier Stage)
ampBlocks.desc: The main voltage gain stage of the amplifier. Here the signal is significantly amplified before being passed to the driver stage, making the VAS the primary determinant of the system's overall gain.

ampBlocks.title: Driver
ampBlocks.desc: Supplies enough current to drive the output (final) stage. The driver acts as a current amplifier and the link between the VAS and the output transistors, so the final stage can work stably.

ampBlocks.title: Final Stage
ampBlocks.desc: The final stage that delivers current and power to the load (headphone). The signal amplified by the previous stages is converted into enough drive capability to run a low-impedance load.

ampBlocks.title: Bias Adjust (Transistor Bias Network)
ampBlocks.desc: Sets the bias current of the output stage so the transistors operate under optimal conditions. In this design the conventional bias diode is replaced with a transistor, making bias more stable across temperature changes while also reducing the circuit size.

ampBlocks.title: DC Servo
ampBlocks.desc: Monitors the DC voltage at the output and slowly corrects the amplifier's input stage, keeping DC offset low without affecting the audio signal at working frequencies.

microamp.psuAlt: Block diagram of the power supply

psuBlocks.title: Charger Module
psuBlocks.desc: Uses a TP4056 module mounted onboard to save PCB space.

psuBlocks.title: Step-Up Converter
psuBlocks.desc: Boosts the battery voltage with high- and low-voltage mode options. Low mode gives longer runtime, while high mode delivers maximum performance.

psuBlocks.title: Charge Pump
psuBlocks.desc: Produces a negative voltage rail so the power supply becomes symmetric (+ and −).

psuBlocks.title: Filter Stage 1
psuBlocks.desc: Consists of capacitors, a ferrite bead, resistors, and more capacitors to suppress ripple and early noise.

psuBlocks.title: Capacitance Multiplier
psuBlocks.desc: Makes a small SMD capacitance behave like a large one, resulting in a cleaner supply.

psuBlocks.title: Filter Stage 2
psuBlocks.desc: Local filters placed near each IC to reduce noise caused by long supply paths.

furuhibi.heroTitle:
Where vintage character meets
modern audio engineering by a clueless, uneducated tinkerer.
furuhibi.heroSub: FuruHibi designs R2R DACs and their supporting software — from firmware, DSP, to cloud presets — as one ecosystem that stays honest to the analog character of sound.
furuhibi.productTitle: A resistor-ladder DAC, fully digitally controlled.
furuhibi.productDesc: Built on the ESP32-S3, FuruHibi R2R combines an R2R DAC path with Bluetooth reception, USB Audio Class, and an OLED display — controlled through a Windows and Android companion app.
furuhibi.productAlt: Architecture diagram of the FuruHibi R2R audio pipeline
furuhibi.ecoTitle: One ecosystem, from hardware to presets.
furuhibi.ecoIntro: Every FuruHibi device is powered by interconnected software — a companion app for device control, DSP to shape the sound, and cloud presets to save the results.

ecoItems.title: Companion App
ecoItems.desc: Windows & Android apps to connect and control FuruHibi devices.

ecoItems.title: DSP
ecoItems.desc: Parametric EQ, loudness, surround and other signal processing, adjusted straight from the browser.

ecoItems.title: Cloud Presets
ecoItems.desc: Save, discover, and share sound presets — synced to your devices anytime.

furuhibi.dspTitle: Fine-tune the way you hear your music.
furuhibi.dspDesc: Parametric EQ, loudness compensation, stereo widening, down to soft clipper — all adjustable straight from the browser-based DSP panel, in real time to the device.
furuhibi.presetsTitle: Discover, save and manage your sound presets.
furuhibi.presetsDesc: Save your favorite DSP configurations to the cloud, explore presets from other users, and apply them to your FuruHibi device anytime.
furuhibi.downloadsTitle: Companion app for Windows and Android.
furuhibi.philIntro: FuruHibi does not chase technology just for specification numbers. We combine musicality, warmth, and simplicity with digital signal processing and modern connectivity.

philItems.desc: Vintage. Heritage. Memory — the sound character of the past, still preserved.
Everyday. Music. Life — present in the everyday act of listening to music.

furuhibi.aboutP1: FuruHibi comes from Japanese: furu (古), meaning "old, ancient, vintage", and hibi (日々), meaning "days". Philosophically, the name conveys "days that have passed" — memories of yesteryear.
furuhibi.aboutP2: For us, audio is not just specifications and measurement figures. Audio is about how music brings out emotion, awakens memories, and accompanies everyday life.
